title.narrative: Tamil Nadu Urban Flagship Investment Program - Project 1

description.narrative: The program will develop priority water supply, sewage and drainage infrastructure in at least 10 cities located within strategic industrial corridors of Tamil Nadu. It will support innovative pilots, including India's first solar-powered sewage treatment plant (STP) to offset greenhouse gas emissions and enhance operational efficiency; strengthen urban governance; and build capacity of state and local institutions to enhance services delivery, environmental sustainability, and climate resilience.

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance strengthened Indicator: 3a. By 2026, minimum 50% of 600 school students, teachers and administrators (with al least 50% women) and 18 women SHGs reported improved awareness on water conservation and hygiene in six project cities (2017 Baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Fully achieved.​ Cumulative: Completed 6 programs in T1 6 ULBs.​
Total 1098 students and staffs participants out of which 803 (73%) were females. Out of 1098, menstrual hygiene awareness program for 418 girl students were covered.​
Awareness program for SHG women: (Target Achieved for SHG women groups in 6 ULBs as per the requirement)​
​Cumulative: Completed 6 awareness programs for 270 SHG women participants from 95 SHGs in 6 ULBs. Since there was a high number of SHGs existing in project areas, we have to inform the SHG groups. So, we were able to reach out to more SHGs (95) instead of 18 as per the GAP indicator. Data Source: Post-awareness campaign sample survey Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance strengthened Indicator: By 2020, at least 80% of technical staff in PDMC (75% participation of female technical staff) trained in the design and implementation of urban infrastructure projects reported improved knowledge and/or skills (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: PDMC's technical staff at the Directorate of Municipal Administration (DMA) have been receiving training on various technical aspects related to the design and implementation of urban infrastructure projects. GIAC has conducted five technical training sessions covering topics such as Water Conservation, Faecal Sludge Management Systems, Technologies in Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs), and Best practices in Urban Water Management. ​
There are a total of 13 sanctioned technical positions in PDMC, including 1 Superintending Engineer, 2 Executive Engineers (EE), 4 Assistant Executive Engineers (AEE), 4 Assistant Engineers (AE), and 2 Droughting Officer. ​
Out of these 13 positions, 6 are currently vacant. Among the 7 filled positions, there are 2 male and 5 female staff members (Female % is 71%) All 7 available technical staff members (including 5 females and 2 males) have undergone technical trainings conducted by GIAC. Thus, 100% of the female staff in PDMC have been trained.​
Similar technical training programs will continue to be provided by GIAC to PDMC's technical staff during the upcoming quarter of 2025.​ Data Source: MAWS annual policy note, and program quarterly progress reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance strengthened Indicator: By 2020, project design and implementation manuals for urban services delivery with applicable standards for PDMC developed (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: This output from the TA has been completed. Design manuals had been submitted by ADB TA​. Additionally, through technical trainings GIAC is also sharing various service and quality standards. Data Source: MAWS annual policy note, and program quarterly progress reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance strengthened Indicator: By 2023, PDMC established in CMA (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Achieved ​
The Project Management and Design Centre (PDMC) was established in the Directorate of Municipal Administration (DMA) in the year 2019 and has been renewed every year since. The latest renewal has been issued vide G.O.(D) No.36, dated 22.01.2025, sanctioning the continuance of 13 temporary posts under PDMC for a period of one year from October 2024 to October 2025. Data Source: MAWS annual policy note, and program quarterly progress reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance strengthened Indicator: By 2023, new database for at least six cities established at urban data and governance improvement cell, with sex-disaggregated data where applicable. (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: UDGIC cell is yet to be operational. ​
The draft design document prepared by GIAC provision for capturing sex disaggregated data has been incorporated. ​
GIAC has collected the sex disaggregated data on staffs, elected representatives and Standing Committee members from 5 ULBs. The staff data with sex disaggregated has been uploaded and published by ULBs in their websites. The same has been reported and recommended to release of Performance Incentive Grant for PI5.( 2023-24) Data Source: MAWS annual policy note, and program quarterly progress reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y
